findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) in test is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: The test patches `time.sleep` to a no-op at line 15 (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`), so the `time.sleep(0.1)` added at line 62 to "give flusher threads time to process after drift change" does nothing. The intended synchronization doesn't happen, so the test relies on timing luck and can be flaky (the single expected message may not have been produced before `step.join()`). Use a real sleep reference captured before patching, or poll for the expected condition with a timeout.

findings.title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for spawn-context processes
findings.body: `self.mp_context.Process` with the "spawn" context creates `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which derives from `BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.Process` (= `multiprocessing.context.Process`). Therefore `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False and neither `process.kill()` in `_ensure_processes_alive` nor `process.terminate()` in `join` is ever executed. Hung flusher processes are never killed before a replacement is spawned, so two processes can flush the same shards concurrently (duplicate segment production), and processes are not terminated on shutdown. Check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` instead.

findings.title: Dead method `_create_process_for_shard`
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(shard)` is never called anywhere after the refactor (restart now goes through `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). Dead code that duplicates restart logic and will silently rot / be misused; remove it.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name: 'shards' vs 'shard'
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards=shard_tag` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `shard=shard_tag`, and `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` uses `shard=<single shard>`. Mixed tag keys/semantics for the same dimension make dashboards and queries inconsistent; pick one key name (and note the value is now a comma-joined list, which also changes tag cardinality/semantics vs. before).

findings.title: Parent process creates one extra SpansBuffer (and Redis connections) per flusher process
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shards` constructs a `SpansBuffer` in the parent and keeps it in `self.buffers`, in addition to the one pickled into the child. On every process restart a new buffer replaces the old entry without closing it, leaking Redis connections in the long-running consumer. Also `submit()` now calls `get_memory_info()` on every buffer, issuing N duplicate INFO calls against the same Redis cluster each submit.

findings.title: New flusher test asserts only counts, and leaks the strategy factory pool
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` checks process counts and that the total number of mapped shards is 4, but never asserts the shard->process mapping is a disjoint partition of the assigned shards (the real correctness property: no shard flushed by two processes, none dropped). It also never calls `fac.shutdown()`, leaving flusher threads/buffers around after the test.
